title: Supplier catalog import times out on 200k-row files
measures: The importer is quadratic in three places (a per-row helper that re-parses the file from the start to find the row's line number, a linear scan of the existing catalog per row, findIndex+splice for duplicate SKUs) and finally does products.push(...out), which throws RangeError above ~120k products on a normal stack. The tempting fix (line = record index + 1, a Set for existing SKUs, a Map with set() for duplicates) is fast but reports wrong line numbers once quoted values span lines or blank lines appear, and lists a duplicated SKU at its first instead of its last position; hidden tests compare exact products, order, line numbers and errors on small hand-built and generated files and on 200k/120k-row files imported in a 1 MB-stack worker under a time budget calibrated with more than 20x headroom.
prompt:
Catalog upload times out for big suppliers

Since we onboarded Holzwerk (their catalog is ~200k rows, ~12 MB) the admin "Upload catalog" page spins and the load balancer returns 504 after 30 s. Smaller suppliers are fine. I timed `importCatalog` locally with generated files: 2k rows 0.3 s, 4k rows 1 s, 8k rows 4 s, so it explodes with size. We need 250k-row files to import comfortably inside the request.

Please keep the result exactly as documented in docs/import-format.md. Suppliers fix their files from the error list, and most descriptions are multi-line quoted text, so `line 1234` must be the line they see in their text editor. The shop team also relies on the documented order of products and on which row wins when a SKU is repeated.
